+----------------------------------------------------------------------+ . ``` ::: ::: ## 7.3 Generating Variables Using Extended Generate The command `egen` is used whenever we want to create variables which require access to some functions (e.g. mean, standard deviation, min). The basic syntax works as follows: ```stata bysort groupvar: egen new_var = function() , options ``` Let's see an example where we create a new variable called *avg_earnings*, which is the mean of earnings for every worker. We will need to reload our data since we dropped many observations above when we used the `keep` command. ::: {#9112ee80 .cell execution_count=18} ``` {.python .cell-code} %%stata clear * use "fake_data.dta", clear ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` . . clear * . use "fake_data.dta", clear . ``` ::: ::: ::: {#d07c5617 .cell execution_count=19} ``` {.python .cell-code} %%stata capture drop avg_earnings bysort workerid: egen avg_earnings = mean(earnings) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` . . capture drop avg_earnings . bysort workerid: egen avg_earnings = mean(earnings) . ``` ::: ::: ::: {#e1ce7d7d .cell execution_count=20} ``` {.python .cell-code} %%stata capture drop total_earnings bysort workerid: egen total_earnings = total(earnings) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` . . capture drop total_earnings . bysort workerid: egen total_earnings = total(earnings) . ``` ::: ::: By definition, these commands will create variables that use information across different observations. You can check the list of available functions by writing `help egen` in the Stata command window. In this documentation, we can see that there are some functions that do not allow for `by`. For example, suppose we want to create the total sum across different variables in the same row. We do this below by taking the sum of *start_year*, *region*, and *treated*. ::: {#7daf4f2e .cell execution_count=21} ``` {.python .cell-code} %%stata cap drop sum_of_vars egen sum_of_vars = rowtotal(start_year region treated) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` . . cap drop sum_of_vars . egen sum_of_vars = rowtotal(start_year region treated) . ``` ::: ::: The variable we are creating for the example has no particular meaning, but what we need to notice is that the function `rowtotal()` only sums the non-missing values in our variables.
